answer: For a poll on a lantern at the inlet, officials randomly select one resident per address from a frozen register. They check each applicant's ID against the selected name, issue one ballot per selected resident, and refuse mismatches or repeats. Extra votes may require recruiting selected residents, costing effort. The rule assumes the register is accurate; shared IDs can enable impersonation, and unselected residents are excluded. The lantern sits at the vertex of a sculpture.
